diagnostic_evidence.quote:
We rigorously prove that this implicit treatment 
is unconditionally BP

issues.failure_explanation: In the implicit scheme, p^{n+1} is a function of z_1 at fixed (rho e)^n, and f(z_1)=kappa(z_1) div u^n with kappa = z_1 z_2 (nu_1-nu_2)/nu, nu_k = 1/(gamma_k (p(z_1)+p_{w,k})). For gas-liquid parameters (e.g. p_{w,2}=6000) and a gas-dominated cell with small rho e, p(z_1) becomes negative as z_1 decreases, so nu_1 and nu_2 take opposite signs on a sub-interval and nu(z_1) has a zero there; kappa, hence F, blows up and is not continuous on [0,1]. The intermediate value argument from F(0)<=0, F(1)>=0 then does not apply, and a root in [0,1] is not guaranteed in general (on each side of the singularity F may keep a fixed sign). The theorem states no hypothesis ensuring f is continuous (e.g. p(z_1)+p_{w,k}>0 for all z_1 in [0,1]), and bisection may converge to the singularity instead of a root.

failure_location.quote:
The continuity of $F(z_1)$ guarantees the 
existence of root $z_1^{n+1} \in [0, 1]$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add and justify a hypothesis guaranteeing continuity of f on [0,1] (e.g. p(z_1)+p_{w,k}>0 for all z_1 in [0,1], i.e. (rho e)^n > max_k p_{w,k}, or a regularized kappa), or give a separate argument for existence in the general case, and state the corresponding restriction on the 'unconditional' claim.
issues.overall_effect: The unconditional BP/existence guarantee for the backward Euler kappa step, and hence for the adaptive Euler/SDIRK2 scheme (adaptive_sdirk2) whose proof is said to be 'similar', is unsupported precisely in the stiff gas-liquid regime the paper targets; the abstract's 'unconditionally BP' claim is unproven.
issues.title: Existence proof for implicit kappa step assumes continuity of F(z_1), which fails when nu(z_1) vanishes
issues.why_classification: The result can be rescued with an extra hypothesis or a contained additional argument, but this genuinely restricts the advertised unconditional guarantee in the gas-liquid regime; no global rearchitecture is needed.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: The solution after BP limiter satisfies \eqref{U_ingp} and maintain the element average of the OEDG solution.

issues.failure_explanation: theta_{z_1} is defined by a case split in which the lower-bound ratio is used whenever m_{i,j} < eps_z. If simultaneously M_{i,j} > 1-eps_z (a cell whose polynomial undershoots 0 and overshoots 1), the upper-bound ratio is ignored, and the scaled solution can still exceed 1-eps_z at some quadrature point, contradicting the claim that the limited solution satisfies (U_ingp).
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Define theta_{z_1} as the minimum of the two ratios (each taken to be 1 when the corresponding bound is not violated), as in standard Zhang-Shu type limiters.
issues.overall_effect: The BP limiter's stated guarantee z_1 in [eps_z, 1-eps_z] at all Gauss-Lobatto points fails in cells violating both bounds.
issues.title: Volume-fraction limiter theta_{z_1} only corrects one bound when both bounds are violated
issues.why_classification: A one-line local correction to the case split restores the guarantee with no loss of any claim.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: complemented by a BP limiter to ensure the BP property of partial densities, pressure, and volume fraction.
For all cases, we simply employ $\Delta t \propto \Delta x$ and $CFL=0.1$.

issues.failure_explanation: The scaling limiter (BP_Z),(BP_P) yields a solution in G^p only if the cell average of the OEDG solution lies in G^p (the formulas for theta and eps_p are meaningless otherwise, e.g. eps_p<0 if p(bar U)<0). The paper asserts the limited solution satisfies (U_ingp) and advertises a BP scheme for partial densities, pressure and volume fraction, but never proves cell-average preservation: no CFL condition or Zhang-Shu type argument is given for the transport RKDG step (with the quasi-conservative non-conservative z_1 discretization), and the implicit kappa step changes z_1 at fixed rho e, so the pointwise pressure p(z_1^{n+1}) can become negative (for Tammann liquid parameters p(z_1) decreases sharply as z_1 decreases), so positivity of the cell-average pressure after that step is not guaranteed either. Only z_1 in [0,1] is proved (Theorem thm:implicit_solver).

failure_location.quote: The solution after BP limiter satisfies \eqref{U_ingp} and maintain the element average of the OEDG solution.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: State the BP guarantee as conditional on cell averages remaining in G^p, and either prove cell-average preservation for the transport step under an explicit CFL condition (and address pressure after the kappa step), or explicitly weaken the abstract/introduction claims to only the volume-fraction bound of the implicit step and the limiter's conditional property.
issues.overall_effect: The claimed BP property of the overall BP-OEDG scheme (in particular pressure positivity and partial-density positivity) is unsupported; it is a conditional property depending on unproven cell-average admissibility.
issues.title: BP guarantee of the full scheme presupposes cell averages in G^p, which is never established
issues.why_classification: A rigorous resolution needs a new, nontrivial cell-average BP argument (or an explicit weakening of the advertised guarantee), but the method and main results remain recognizable.

issues.failure_explanation: G requires z_1 rho_1 > 0 and z_2 rho_2 > 0 strictly. U^{(1)} has z_2 rho_2 = 0 and U^{(2)} has z_1 rho_1 = 0, so neither lies in G, and the claimed membership verification is false; the appendix therefore does not, as written, exhibit two elements of G whose midpoint leaves G. (The midpoint computation itself, giving c^2<0, is correct.)

failure_location.quote:
Thus, $\mathbf{U}^{(1)}$ is physically 
 admissible and belongs to $\mathcal{G}$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Perturb the two states to have small positive partial densities of the absent phase (z_1 = 1-eps, z_2 = eps and vice versa); by continuity the midpoint still has c^2 < 0 and the endpoints then satisfy all strict inequalities.
issues.overall_effect: The stated non-convexity demonstration for G is not valid as written, weakening the motivation for replacing G by G^p.
issues.title: Appendix A counterexample states have zero partial densities and so do not belong to G as defined
issues.why_classification: A routine local perturbation of the example restores the demonstration with no loss of content.
